answer: The sonnet cap is upheld at intake and ivory shows the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a island tag. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 26 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
